title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site SOPs, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for the Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation set: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and a canonical list of top support issues with fixes. It is intended for DevEx authors, SDK owners, technical writers, and on-call support engineers.

Scope:
- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts and reference templates (serverless, backend, client integrations)
- API examples (generation, chat, embeddings, function/tool-calling)
- Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle, publishing workflow, rollback)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage + KB entries)

Conventions and style
- Audience: engineers integrating Redwood Inference services; examples must compile and use the public SDKs.
- Tone: technical, concise, prescriptive.
- Structure: every page must include: Intro, When to use, Code examples, Troubleshooting, Ownership/contacts, Related pages.
- Files: use kebab-case filenames, include year in filename (e.g., sdk-quickstart-python-2026.json).

Section 1 \u2014 SDK Guides (standards)
1. Required pages for each SDK (Python / TS / Go):
   - Getting started (install + auth)
   - Quickstart: hello-world generation
   - Advanced usage: streaming, function-calling, structured outputs
   - Performance: batching, retries, connection pooling examples
   - Migration notes: breaking changes and changelog pointers
   - API reference link to autogenerated docs

2. Minimum content checklist (must be present in each SDK guide):
   - Example: pip/npm/go install commands
   - Auth: how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY or env var (with example CLI export commands)
   - Example requests for text generation, chat, embeddings (sync + streaming)
   - Error handling patterns and recommended retry/backoff
   - Tests/CI snippet showing how to run unit tests that depend on mocked SDK clients

3. Ownership and release rules:
   - SDK owner (code) and DevEx owner (docs) must be listed on the top of the page.
   - Any code changes that affect the public surface must trigger a docs PR.
   - Release checklist: update migration notes, run examples in CI, smoke test on docs staging site.

Section 2 \u2014 Quickstarts and templates
Purpose: provide drop-in templates for common integration patterns so customers can go from sign-up to a working integration in <30 minutes.

Canonical quickstarts (priority):
- Python backend: text generation + caching (template: fastapi + uvicorn)
- Next.js client: streaming chat UI (examples with SDK + SSE fallback)
- Embeddings pipeline: ingestion -> embeddings -> vector db (Postgres + pgvector example)
- Serverless function: AWS Lambda + Redwood API (cold-start guidance)

Template rules:
- Keep templates minimal (<= 200 lines where possible).
- Include a README with deploy steps and cost/latency notes.
- Add a small tests folder with one integration smoke test that runs in CI against a staging API key.

Section 3 \u2014 API examples
- Provide short, copy-pasteable snippets demonstrating: generation, chat with system messages, streaming output, function/tool calling, embeddings + nearest-neighbors example, and reranking.
- Include both REST/HTTP and SDK examples for each common language.
- Mark examples with expected token cost and approximate latency for the curated model (e.g., redwood-open-7b, 512 context).

Example snippet (Python generation):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-open-7b", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'", max_tokens=64)
print(resp.text)
```

Section 4 \u2014 Docs site operating procedures (SOPs)
Purpose: keep the docs site stable, auditable, and fast to update.

Workflow (content lifecycle):
1. Draft locally using the docs template (MDX/Markdown) and run local dev server.
2. Submit a docs PR against the devex/docs repo; include reviewer from DevEx team and the SDK owner.
3. CI must run: linting, link-checks, build, and smoke examples execution (using a staging API key).
4. On approval, merge to main -> automated deploy to staging. Author must perform a quick smoke test on staging.
5. When staging sign-off complete, trigger the scheduled production deploy window or request emergency deploy in the DocOps channel.

Rollback and emergency fix guidance:
- If a public change causes customer-impacting regressions (broken examples, 5xx docs API errors), open a PagerDuty incident and revert the docs commit via the rollback button in Vercel/Netlify.
- Hotfix procedure: branch from main, apply minimal fix, PR with high-priority tag, and request expedited review.

Publishing cadence and changelog:
- DocOps publishes a weekly changelog post listing merged docs PRs and major updates.
- Major how-to changes should be tagged with migration notes and an example diff.

Section 5 \u2014 Top support issues and canonical fixes (KB)
This is the canonical triage list DevEx and Support use to resolve common customer problems. Each entry should be a short KB page with: symptom, root cause, quick fix, longer remediation, and links to examples.

Canonical issues (current top 10):
1. Authentication failures (401):
   - Symptom: 401 on all API calls.
   - Quick fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, correct env var name, no trailing whitespace. Run `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` to validate.
2. Streaming timeouts in browser clients:
   - Symptom: streaming tokens stop after ~10s or do not arrive.
   - Quick fix: ensure SSE/TCP connections allowed by proxy; add reconnect/backoff logic; verify SDK streaming fallback (chunked) enabled.
3. High latency on small-batch workloads:
   - Symptom: single-request latency > SLO (500ms for short prompts).
   - Quick fix: enable background batching for the route or use a lower-latency model variant (redwood-inference-low-latency).
4. Embeddings mismatch vs. vector DB results:
   - Symptom: nearest-neighbor results differ from expected sample outputs.
   - Quick fix: confirm embedding model and normalization used in ingestion and query are identical; check dimension mismatch errors.
5. Rate limit errors (429) during bursts:
   - Symptom: 429s during unpredictable bursts.
   - Quick fix: implement client-side exponential backoff and jitter; increase quota or request burst capacity for dedicated customers.
6. SDK version compatibility errors:
   - Symptom: Type errors or missing method after SDK upgrade.
   - Quick fix: consult the migration notes page and pin to supported minor version in package.json/pyproject.toml.
7. Function calling / tool mismatch:
   - Symptom: model returns free-text instead of invoking function.
   - Quick fix: ensure function schema matches the SDK call signature and enable tool-calling mode in the client.
8. CORS errors in browser integrations:
   - Symptom: preflight failures when using client-side SDK.
   - Quick fix: recommend server-side proxy for production; update allowed origins in console for dev testing.
9. Incorrect token accounting vs. billing:
   - Symptom: customer reports discrepancy between tokens seen in logs and billing.
   - Quick fix: confirm whether caching or prefix trimming was applied; check per-token rounding policy and multi-part streaming boundaries.
10. Example code that relies on internal-only models:
   - Symptom: examples fail with 403 or model-not-found.
   - Quick fix: replace internal model names with public curated variants and note model equivalence in migration notes.

KB maintenance rules:
- Each KB entry must include reproduction steps, a minimal failing example, and a verified fix that an engineer has run.
- KB pages should be linked from relevant SDK guides and quickstarts.
- Quarterly review: DevEx team rotates ownership of the top-10 list to validate it matches current on-call telemetry.

Section 6 \u2014 CI and testing for docs
Minimum CI checks for docs PRs:
- Markdown/MDX linting
- Linkchecker on internal and external links
- Build the site and confirm no runtime errors in console logs
- Run smoke examples with a staging API key and fail the PR if examples error

Example CI step (bash):
- run: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$STAGING_DOCS_KEY
- run: pytest tests/smoke_examples.py::test_python_quickstart --maxfail=1 -q

Section 7 \u2014 Ownership and escalation
- DevEx team: primary owners for content; contact: #devex-docs in Slack.
- SDK owners: maintain code examples and migrations.
- Support/On-call: triage customer tickets and add new KB items.
- Escalation path: Support -> DevEx owner -> SDK owner -> SRE (if infra-related).

Appendix: Templates and snippets
- Quickstart README template, code of conduct for examples (no production secrets), and a changelog header must be included in each new quickstart repo.

README quick template (top):
{{project-name}}
Purpose: One-sentence description
Prereqs: Node 18+/Python 3.10+, REDWOOD_API_KEY
Quickstart: steps to run locally and expected output

Contact and feedback
- For doc edits, open a PR and add the `doc:req` label.
- For missing examples or new quickstart requests, file an issue in the devex/docs repo and tag the DevEx on-call.
